name: TX-29
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Sylvia Garcia running with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger has raised no money
model.rationale: Garcia holds a D+17 district with incumbency advantages and roughly $1 million raised plus outside support, while Fierro has shown no fundraising footprint. Markets price Garcia around 96%, consistent with a safe Democratic rating.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a single-digit race or major outside spending against Garcia would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sylvia Garcia seeks another term in a Houston-area district that leans Democratic by about 17 points. She enters the general election as a well-established incumbent, having won renomination and built a substantial financial advantage, including outside support on her side of the ledger.

Republican Martha Fierro faces steep odds: she has reported no fundraising and no outside backing, and no independent polls of the race are available. Prediction markets give Garcia roughly a 96% chance of winning. The fundamentals, money, and market pricing all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being the absence of direct polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
